open_obligations: Recompute ASD for Khan et al.'s consultancy runs, if both correct and incorrect assignments were run.
Check that Khan et al.'s debates meet Sudhir et al.'s definition of simultaneous debate.
Check whether the debate-over-consultancy ordering survives under ASD.

out.other_title: Human judges 88% with debate vs 78% consultancy; LLM judges 76% vs 54% (naive 60% / 48%)
out.rationale: Khan et al. report, for the most persuasive models, non-expert judge accuracy of 88% (humans) and 76% (LLMs) with debate versus 78% and 54% with consultancy. Sudhir et al. argue that judge accuracy relative to consultancy is the wrong alignment metric and that ASD, the score difference between arguing the true and false answer, is equivalent to judge accuracy for simultaneous debate but not for consultancy, so the baseline comparison in previous debate experiments is incorrect; if Khan et al.'s debates are simultaneous, only the consultancy side of the comparison would be affected.
out.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: whether debate's judge-accuracy gain over consultancy measures how much a protocol rewards truth-telling

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The authors argue judge accuracy relative to a Consultancy baseline is the wrong metric for evaluating scalable oversight protocols from an alignment perspective, and define ASD as the difference between the score an agent earns arguing for the true answer and for the false answer (e.g. judge belief 0.8 for a truthful agent and 0.6 for a lying one gives log 0.8 minus log 0.6, about 0.29). They state ASD is equivalent to judge accuracy for simultaneous debate but not for Consultancy, so the baseline comparison in previous debate experiments is incorrect.
title: Agent score difference (ASD) replaces judge accuracy as the protocol metric
